record.paper_title: Open problems in microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion
record.context_brief: Time-odd mean-field contributions to collective mass
record.original_question: How large are the contributions of time-odd mean-field components induced by the time evolution of the mean field to the collective mass in large-amplitude collective motion, and how can those effects be evaluated reliably within modern nuclear energy density functionals rather than being omitted as they are in the usual cranking mass?

evidence.quote: In spite of these efforts, it may be fair to say that we are still far from a full understanding of the time-odd effects.
Thus, it remains as a great subject for future to evaluate the time-odd mean-field effects on the collective mass using energy density functionals currently under active development.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a self-bound, finite quantum many-body system (e.g., an atomic nucleus) described by a nuclear energy density functional (EDF) that depends on both time-even and time-odd local densities and currents (so as to respect Galilean invariance). Suppose the system undergoes large-amplitude collective motion along a slow collective coordinate q(t), and let the time-dependent mean-field generated by the EDF support the corresponding moving Slater determinant |Φ(q, p)⟩, where p is the momentum conjugate to q. Define the collective mass M(q) as the inertia appearing in the collective Hamiltonian H_coll(q, p) = p^2/(2 M(q)) + V(q) obtained from a fully self-consistent adiabatic / adiabatic-self-consistent-collective-coordinate (ASCC) reduction of the time-dependent mean-field dynamics. The standard Inglis–Belyaev cranking mass M_cr(q) is obtained by neglecting the time-odd components of the moving mean field (the rearrangement of the mean field induced by the time evolution of the densities), and is known to underestimate M(q).

Problem: Quantitatively determine the magnitude of the contribution ΔM(q) := M(q) − M_cr(q) arising from the time-odd components of the mean field that are induced by the time evolution of the densities, for nuclear EDFs of current interest (e.g., Skyrme-type or relativistic/covariant EDFs that include all time-odd terms required by Galilean/Lorentz invariance). Develop a reliable, fully self-consistent method—rather than the cranking approximation that omits them—to evaluate these time-odd mean-field effects on the collective mass for large-amplitude collective motion (such as fission, shape coexistence, and low-energy heavy-ion reactions), and characterize how ΔM(q)/M_cr(q) depends on the chosen functional and on the collective coordinate.
artifact.category_tag: Nuclear energy density functionals and collective mass
artifact.status_search_result: The literature confirms that time-odd mean-field components contribute substantially to the collective mass and that the cranking formula systematically misses them. Methods such as ASCC and adiabatic TDHF(B) include such effects in principle, and studies (e.g., Hinohara et al., PTP 2006; Frontiers in Physics 2020 review) report sizeable enhancements of the collective inertia (often tens of percent) over the cranking value. However, a fully systematic, reliable evaluation within modern Skyrme/relativistic EDFs containing all required time-odd terms remains an active research program rather than a settled result, so the problem is best classified as still open.

status_evidence.title: Effects of Time-Odd Components in Mean Field on Large Amplitude Collective Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: The collective mass is significantly increased by the time-odd components of the moving mean field, beyond the cranking approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Time-odd mean-field components substantially enhance the collective mass relative to the cranking formula.

status_evidence.title: Collective Inertial Masses in Nuclear Reactions (Frontiers in Physics, 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: The cranking formula fails when the time-odd components exist; ASCC inertial functions contain contributions of the time-odd components of the mean field, which are ignored in the cranking formula.
status_evidence.claim: Reliable evaluation of time-odd contributions to the collective mass within modern EDFs is still an active research topic.

status_evidence.title: Density functional approaches to collective phenomena in nuclei (PTEP 2012)
status_evidence.snippet: Galilean symmetry requires time-odd densities in the EDF; their effect on collective dynamics requires self-consistent treatment beyond cranking.
status_evidence.claim: Self-consistent inclusion of all time-odd EDF terms in collective mass calculations remains a challenge.
